ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Bone health

A 62-year-old woman on long-term phenytoin develops low-trauma fractures and biochemical evidence of vitamin D deficiency. She has no malabsorptive illness. Which drug-related mechanism can contribute to her skeletal problem?

  1. Increased vitamin D metabolism from hepatic enzyme induction
  2. Direct vitamin D receptor activation
  3. Complete inhibition of renal calcium excretion
  4. Increased intestinal calcium uptake in every patient
  5. Permanent stimulation of osteoblast formation
Answer and explanation

Increased vitamin D metabolism from hepatic enzyme induction

Chronic enzyme-inducing antiseizure therapy can reduce vitamin D availability and adversely affect bone health.

Option explanations

Increased vitamin D metabolism from hepatic enzyme induction: Chronic enzyme-inducing antiseizure therapy can reduce vitamin D availability and adversely affect bone health.

Direct vitamin D receptor activation: Activation would not explain vitamin D deficiency.

Complete inhibition of renal calcium excretion: This is not the characteristic mechanism.

Increased intestinal calcium uptake in every patient: This does not explain deficiency-related skeletal disease.

Permanent stimulation of osteoblast formation: This is not a recognized protective effect of phenytoin.
